role_sought: Municipal councillor, Antwerp (Volksunie candidate on the CVP–VU cartel list 'Antwerpen 94')
detail: First candidacy; he later sat briefly on the Berchem district council (1996–1997).

role_sought: Member of the Chamber, Antwerp constituency (N-VA list leader)
detail: The N-VA won a single Chamber seat nationwide, in West Flanders, which led it to form an electoral cartel with CD&V in February 2004.

role_sought: Member of the Flemish Parliament, Antwerp constituency (4th on the CD&V–N-VA cartel list)
vote_share: 17,665 preference votes; CD&V–N-VA list 271,204 votes (25.09% of valid votes in the constituency), 9 seats
detail: Official results of the FPS Home Affairs (IBZ) election results service.

role_sought: Municipal councillor, Antwerp (3rd on the CD&V–N-VA list)
detail: Became the only N-VA member of the Antwerp city council from January 2007. He was also elected to the Berchem district council but chose not to sit.

role_sought: Member of the Chamber, Antwerp constituency (2nd on the CD&V–N-VA cartel list)
vote_share: 41,962 preference votes; CD&V–N-VA list 327,558 votes (29.28% of valid votes in the constituency), 8 seats
detail: Official IBZ results. He left the Chamber after returning to the Flemish Parliament in 2009.

role_sought: Member of the Flemish Parliament, Antwerp constituency (N-VA list leader)
vote_share: 123,155 preference votes; N-VA list 180,246 votes (16.37% of valid votes in the constituency), 6 seats
detail: Official IBZ results. N-VA's first election as an independent party after the end of the cartel with CD&V; it won 16 seats in the Flemish Parliament and joined the Peeters II government. On the same day he was elected to the European Parliament from 13th place on the N-VA list but did not take the seat, which went to Frieda Brepoels.

role_sought: Directly elected senator, Dutch-speaking electoral college (N-VA list leader)
result: Elected (did not take up the directly elected seat; sat as a community senator)
vote_share: 785,776 preference votes; N-VA list 1,268,780 votes (31.69% of valid votes in the Dutch-speaking electoral college), 9 seats
detail: Official IBZ results. The N-VA became the largest party in Belgium; De Wever's preference-vote total was the highest in the Dutch-speaking electorate. He was then appointed royal informateur.

opponent: Patrick Janssens (outgoing mayor, sp.a–CD&V 'stadslijst': 28.58%, 17 seats; 49,859 preference votes)
detail: Formed a coalition of N-VA, CD&V and Open Vld, putting the socialists into opposition in Antwerp for the first time in about 90 years.

role_sought: Member of the Chamber, Antwerp constituency (N-VA list leader)
vote_share: 314,650 preference votes; N-VA list 449,531 votes (39.38% of valid votes in the constituency), 11 seats
detail: Official IBZ results. N-VA's best result, with 33 Chamber seats nationwide.

result: Re-elected; second term as mayor from January 2019
detail: Formed a coalition of N-VA, Open Vld and sp.a.

role_sought: Member of the Flemish Parliament, Antwerp constituency (N-VA list leader; candidate for Minister-President)
vote_share: 242,386 preference votes; N-VA list 361,403 votes (31.82% of valid votes in the constituency), 12 seats
detail: Official IBZ results. The N-VA remained the largest party in Flanders but fell to about 25% as Vlaams Belang advanced; De Wever did not become Minister-President.

role_sought: Member of the Chamber, Antwerp constituency (N-VA list leader and candidate for Prime Minister)
result: Elected; became Prime Minister on 3 February 2025
vote_share: 255,446 preference votes; N-VA list 368,877 votes (30.97% of valid votes in the constituency), 8 of 24 seats
detail: Official IBZ results. The N-VA stayed the largest party in the Chamber and in Flanders, narrowly ahead of Vlaams Belang (249,826 votes in the Antwerp constituency).

result: Re-elected; sworn in for a third term on 20 January 2025, exercise of the office handed over on becoming Prime Minister
vote_share: N-VA just over 37% (VRT); 59,309 preference votes, the highest in the province of Antwerp
detail: PVDA came second with just over 20% and Vooruit third with almost 13%; Open VLD lost its seats. The N-VA formed a coalition with Vooruit.
